So - how could I even *remotely* attempt to *repair* a glass piece that got broken?

Do you happen to know what type of glass it is? Their are 2 main types that people create with: boro and soft (soda-lime).

If it is soft glass, then you could preheat it in the oven and use a torch as you are talking about. If it is boro, you have a high risk of thermal shock if it isn't pre-heated to the correct temp, that and you will more than likely need to use an oxy accelerant to get the torch up to the correct temp as well.

To preheat, place oven and set it as high as it will go, unless it is over 850F. You will need to introduce the torch from the tip of the flame, so you introduce the heat slowly. Start away from the cracked area first and slowly work your way over the crack. It should seal together. Put back in the over as soon as possible and keep your finger crossed. after a while turn the over off and don't open it until it cools completely.

You are likely to loose it not going through proper annealing cycles, but this is your best option if you don't know a lampworker.
